note_claims.claim: The patient presents with red, swollen left shin since Tuesday.
The redness started on Wednesday morning, following a scratch on the roses on Tuesday (patient initially stated Tuesday).
The patient reports warmth and soreness in the affected area.
There are no blisters or dark patches present.
The patient's temperature this morning was 37.6 °C (self-measured).
The patient feels systemically well, with no rigors, vomiting, or confusion.
There is no swelling of the other leg.
The patient has Type 2 diabetes.
The patient is taking Metformin 500 mg twice daily.
The patient has no known drug allergies.
The patient has had penicillins without problems.
Erythema is present over the anterior left shin, approximately 10 cm across, with a small central scratch.
No blistering or necrosis is visible.
The clinical impression is Cellulitis of the left lower leg (Eron class I) following a scratch.
Flucloxacillin 500 mg is prescribed once daily for 7 days.
Flucloxacillin should be taken on an empty stomach, an hour before food or two hours after.
The margin of erythema should be marked with a pen.
The patient should keep the leg raised when sitting.
The patient should take paracetamol for pain.
No routine review is needed.
Same-day contact (or 111) is required if redness spreads beyond the marked line.
Same-day contact (or 111) is required if the patient develops a high temperature, rigors, feels very unwell, or confused.
Call 999 if the patient is very unwell.

transcript_facts.fact: The patient initially stated the redness started on Tuesday, but corrected this to Wednesday morning after mentioning he was gardening on Tuesday and scratched the leg on roses.
The clinician observed a red area on the front of the left shin, approximately 10 cm across, with a small scratch in the middle.
The patient reported the area was warm.
The relative reported no blisters or dark patches.
The patient reported the area was sore, but not terrible.
The patient reported a temperature of 37.6 °C this morning.
The patient stated he felt all right and had no systemic symptoms like shivering, sickness, or confusion.
The patient confirmed there was no swelling in the other leg.
The patient has Type 2 diabetes and is taking Metformin 500 milligrams twice a day.
The patient stated he has no known drug allergies.
The relative stated she is allergic to penicillin.
The patient confirmed he has had penicillin and amoxicillin plenty of times without problems.
The clinician prescribed Flucloxacillin 500 milligrams four times a day for seven days.
The clinician instructed the patient to take the medication on an empty stomach, an hour before food or two hours after.
The clinician instructed the relative to draw around the edge of the redness with a pen to check for spreading.
The clinician advised the patient to keep the leg raised when sitting and take paracetamol for pain.
The clinician requested the patient send a photo or have another video call in 48 hours.
Safety netting instructions state that if redness spreads beyond the marked line, the patient should call for a same-day appointment or 111 if closed.
Safety netting instructions state that if the patient has a high temperature, shivers, feels very unwell, or confused, they should call for a same-day appointment or 111 if closed.
Safety netting instructions state that if the patient is very unwell, they should call 999.
